# Page 2^page=2
©Idaho State University, 2020 SCOPE AND CONTENT NOTE The Arney papers consist primarily of correspondence, both personal and political in nature, speeches, and some financial items, during his tenure as personal secretary and political confidant to Fred T. Dubois, 1903-1906; however, the collection covers the period from 1900- 1926. Once part of the Dubois Family Papers, the Arney papers were separated during processing and designated as its own collection. ARRANGEMENT The collection is arranged in two series: Series I contains correspondence written during the period 1900-1914, and is arranged chronologically. Series II contains addresses, financial records, newspaper clippings, and notes. The Arney Papers were once part of the Dubois Papers, but were separated out during processing; the original order is unknown.

# Page 3^page=3
©Idaho State University, 2020 BIOGRAPHICAL NOTE Charles E. Arney was born in Iowa July 22, 1866, to Ira R. and Sarah Ann (Beeson) Arney. He completed three years of high school and in 1887 moved to Idaho, and married Nell Gertrude in 1889; they had two surviving sons, twin boys, Ward J., and Charles E. Arney. Arney worked in a variety of jobs including principal of Eagle Rock schools, as a clerk for the State Land Board, Boise [Id], the railroad in Spokane [Wa], and, from 1901-1907, as Fred T. Dubois’s personal secretary and political confidant.

# Page 4^page=4
©Idaho State University, 2020 CHRONOLOGY 1866 Born July 22 in Marshall County, Iowa 1880 Lived in Iowa Township, Marshall County, Iowa 1887 Moved to Idaho c. 1887 Principal, Eagle Rock Schools, Idaho 1888 Married Nell Gertrude (Arney), Corvalis, Oregon, June 28 1891-1892 Editor, Pocatello Tribune 1893 Elected Probate Judge in first election held in Bannock County, Idaho 1900 Appointed to the State of Idaho Land Department as Clerk, State Land Board 1901 Appointed Warden of the Idaho State Penitentiary, January 29 1902 Assistant to Senator Fred Dubois from Idaho 1903-1906 Personal secretary to Senator Fred T. Dubois 1910 Newspaper Correspondent, Green Meadow, Idaho 1920 Supervisor, Railroad Office, Spokane, Washington 1930 Industrial Agent, Steam Railroad, Opportunity Township, Spokane, Washington 1940 Moved to Pocatello, Idaho 1941 Appointed Coordinator of Priorities to the Idaho mining industry 1942 Appointed Coordinator of Civil Defense in Idaho State University Library 1944 Died March 8, Los Angeles [Ca]; buried, Mountain View Cemetery, Pocatello, Idaho
